title: The branch-PR guard demanded a pull request for a branch that no longer exists

first_order.what_broke: branch-pr-guard.py reported that ci/automerge-without-gh-cli was pushed with no pull request. The branch had already been merged and deleted on GitHub; gh pr create then failed with 'No commits between main and ..., Head ref must be a branch'.
first_order.receipt: git ls-remote --heads origin ci/automerge-without-gh-cli returns nothing, while refs/remotes/origin/ci/automerge-without-gh-cli was still present locally. origin/main already carries the fix at cancel-ci-on-pr-close.yml:52 and automerge.yml:58.

cause_chain: The guard treated a local refs/remotes/origin/<name> as proof the branch exists on the remote.
A merged-and-deleted branch leaves its remote-tracking ref behind until somebody prunes, so the local ref outlives the remote branch.
CLASS: a guard that asks the local cache a question about a remote produces confident false findings, and a guard that cries wolf gets ignored.

second_order.note: RUN 2026-08-19 across rule-guard.py, push-pr-fence.py, branch-pr-guard.py and tool-drip-guard.py: 11 ref-reading call sites. Ten ask a LOCAL question (what branch am I on, does this sha exist here) and answer it locally, which is correct. Only branch-pr-guard.py:144 asked a question about the REMOTE and read the local cache — that is this incident. No siblings.

third_order.mechanism: The guard now asks git ls-remote, and when the branch is gone it deletes the stale remote-tracking ref itself rather than reporting a finding. A probe failure returns None and passes, so a network outage can never manufacture a block.

grade.signature: a guard reading a remote-tracking ref as remote state
